messages.subject: Help on reporting
messages.body_plain:
Dear Rattle users,

I have been using rattle for the past 2 months and it is one of the
best analytical tool that I have ever used. I am thinking of
developing an analytical package that would involve rattle to generate
and publish automated reports to the end users. i.e. strategic reports
at CEO levels, tactical reports at senior manager levels, operational
reports at field level. Guidelines with the details of technical
infrastructure would be most welcome.

--

Thanks and Regards,
Rajesh Kumar

Co-Founder & Managing Director
Aaum Research & Analytics
email: rajesh...@aaumanalytics.com
visit us online at www.aaumanalytics.com <http://www.aaumanalytics.com>

The woods are lovely dark and deep, but I have promises to keep, and
miles to go before I sleep - Robert Frost

messages.subject: Re: Help on reporting
messages.body_plain:
Hi Rajesh,

Rattle is slowly getting some reporting support (through the Report
button in the toolbar) but it is very experimental. It is using
odfWeave. Users are invited to submit sample ODF templates to help
this effort.

odfWeave and Sweave are excellent tools for generating reports from R.

A draft chapter from my data mining survival guide with a little guide
to generating OpenOffice (and hence MS/Word) documents from R is
available.  The HTLM version of the chapter is at

    http://datamining.togaware.com/survivor/Reporting.html

In particular, see the Getting Started section there for a simple
tutorial that will get you started in 1 minute or less (assuming you
have OpenOffice and R installed).

(I see some conversion problems in the HTML - will be fixed at some
stage)

odfWeave allows auto inclusion of results from R commands, R tables,
and plots from R.

Note that the data mining survival guide (PDF and HTML versions) uses
Sweave (and LaTeX) to automatically generate screen shots and display
output from the R commands.

Regards,
Graham

messages.subject: Re: Help on reporting
messages.body_plain:
Sorry David - I did not mean to get you to question your sanity :-)

I changed the Web page before you had a chance to look at it again!

What I meant in the email was that I went to my actual odt file and
cut the text from there and pasted it into the email message I
sent.

And I also fixed the web page - because it is generated from LaTeX and
there are a couple of tricks to get the example into LateX without
Sweave interpreting it and thus turning into the output from R rather
than the example, I did end up with two "ee"s accidently.

I'm still figuring out the font stuff - I would have thought the
odfWeave processing using a fixed width font on all its generated
stuff, and I see comments that it does, but it does not seem to.

Keyboard macros sound like a good idea. If you get a moment to jot
down what one does to do that I'll add it to the page.

Regards,
Graham
